title: Trump Army shuts down entire social media accounts because of one post featuring Democrat war hero Sen. Tammy Duckworth
description_short: Trump Army shuts down entire social media accounts because of one post featuring Democrat war hero Sen. Tammy Duckworth
description_medium: A TrumpFile timeline headed April 13, 2026 says Army Secretary Dan Driscoll ordered Soldier for Life’s accounts offline on an unknown date after the unit posted a tribute to Senator Tammy Duckworth; it says the post and several accounts were removed April 13. The page quotes an Army explanation about accounts lacking qualified public-affairs staff but also attributes the decision to backlash. The Hill link was inaccessible, and no order or restoration record was available.
description_long: After Soldier for Life posted a tribute to Senator Tammy Duckworth, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll ordered the unit’s social-media accounts taken offline, according to the supplied summary of The Hill’s April 15, 2026 report. The post highlighted Duckworth’s life and military service; critics objected to an Army tribute to the Illinois Democrat and Iraq War veteran. A Defense Department source told the paper that Driscoll acted after the negative reaction. The Army gave a different explanation, saying the accounts were not directly managed by qualified public-affairs personnel and were being removed under a broader review. The report also described a December 2025 Army directive requiring accounts without an assigned public-affairs professional to deactivate and archive by February 28, 2026. The accounts were taken offline, but the supplied article summary does not establish whether the Duckworth post alone caused the order or whether the unit was already covered by that directive. It also does not say whether or when the accounts returned. The linked Hill article returned HTTP 403 in this focused read, so those details remain grounded in the supplied packet rather than a fresh accessible copy.

title: Moodys Chief Economist Confirms Tariffs Have Done Significant Damage to US Economy
description_short: Moodys Chief Economist Confirms Tariffs Have Done Significant Damage to US Economy
description_medium: On May 6, 2026 Moodys Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi published a note stating the data are definitive that Trumps tariffs have done significant damage to the economy. A Congressional Democratic study released the same month found American households will pay an average of 2512 dollars in tariff costs in 2026, up 44 percent from 1745 in 2025, while consumers already face elevated costs from the U.S.-Iran war driving up energy prices.
description_long: CNBC’s February 23, 2026 report examined the trade fallout after the Supreme Court struck down President Trump’s tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. The administration announced new tariffs of up to 15% under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974; the article says that authority limits them to 150 days without congressional approval. Moody’s Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi told CNBC that uncertainty could lead businesses to invest and hire less, while foreign governments might shift trade away from the United States. The report also describes possible use of other tariff authorities, while noting that future measures and their effects remained uncertain. It does not establish that Zandi published the May 6 statement in the supplied synopsis or verify the separate household-cost estimate attributed to a congressional study. Those claims need their own sources before this entry can present them as confirmed findings.

title: New York AG Secures Court Order: Trump to Pay $2 Million for Misuse of Trump Foundation Funds
description_short: New York AG Secures Court Order: Trump to Pay $2 Million for Misuse of Trump Foundation Funds

description_long: New York Attorney General Letitia James announced on November 7, 2019, that a state court had ordered Donald Trump to pay $2 million in damages for using Trump Foundation funds to influence the 2016 presidential primaries. Trump admitted to personally misusing charitable assets and agreed to restrictions on future charitable service.
